name: X-linked deafness (POU3F4, DFNX2)
aliases: X-linked mixed deafness with stapes gusher

clinicalPearls: The commonest X-linked form of hereditary hearing loss, caused by variants at or deletions involving POU3F4
Affected males show a progressive mixed hearing loss, with carrier females sometimes mildly and variably affected
Imaging characteristically shows incomplete partition type III with a deficient bony plate between the lateral internal auditory canal and the basal cochlea
This bony deficiency creates an abnormal communication that predisposes to a perilymph gusher if stapes surgery is attempted
The conductive component often reflects a third-window effect rather than fixation, so stapedotomy is contraindicated and typically harmful
Cochlear implantation is possible but carries a heightened risk of a cerebrospinal-fluid gusher requiring specific surgical planning
Recognising the radiological signature is essential to avoid inappropriate middle-ear surgery
reference.pathophysiology: POU3F4 encodes a transcription factor essential for normal development of the mesenchyme surrounding the inner ear. Loss of function disrupts formation of the bony architecture at the fundus of the internal auditory canal and cochlear base, producing the incomplete partition type III malformation in which the modiolus and the bony separation between the internal auditory canal and the cochlea are deficient. This defect allows abnormal communication of cerebrospinal fluid and perilymph, generating a third-window conductive component and the characteristic tendency to gush under surgical manipulation, while progressive sensorineural loss reflects associated cochlear dysfunction. As an X-linked disorder, hemizygous males are more severely and consistently affected than heterozygous females.
additionalDifferentials: Otosclerosis with genuine stapes fixation and a Carhart notch
Enlarged vestibular aqueduct and other third-window lesions
Other X-linked or autosomal causes of mixed hearing loss
Cochlear incomplete partition types I and II
additionalInvestigations: High-resolution temporal bone imaging to identify incomplete partition type III
Pure-tone audiometry documenting the mixed and progressive pattern
Tympanometry and acoustic reflexes to help distinguish third-window from fixation
POU3F4 sequencing and copy-number analysis for deletions
Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials or other third-window assessment when indicated
Preoperative planning imaging when cochlear implantation is considered
redFlags: Planned stapes surgery in a mixed loss without imaging, risking a perilymph gusher
Progressive loss of useful hearing despite amplification
Radiological modiolar deficiency indicating gusher risk at implantation
Family history suggesting further at-risk male relatives needing counselling
reference.prognosis: Hearing loss is progressive and mixed, and while stapes surgery is contraindicated, carefully planned cochlear implantation can rehabilitate advanced sensorineural loss despite the gusher risk.
pitfalls: Mistaking the third-window air-bone gap for otosclerosis and proceeding to stapedotomy
Operating without temporal bone imaging in a mixed hereditary loss
Underestimating cerebrospinal-fluid gusher risk during implantation
Failing to offer genetic counselling to at-risk relatives
